title: The Second Book of Samuel Timeline
sub: The LORD's Covenant With David · Bathsheba, Absalom, and a Fractured House
desc: David's reign rises from civil war to an eternal covenant promise, then unravels through his affair with Bathsheba, a son's rape of his sister, and Absalom's rebellion — a king who wins every war on his borders but loses control of his own household.

eras.label: Era One · 2 Samuel 1
eras.name: David's Lament for Saul and Jonathan
eras.dates: News of Saul's death is met not with relief but with a genuine, grief-stricken funeral song, and the messenger who claims credit for killing Saul is executed on the spot

events.title: How the Mighty Have Fallen — David's Lament
events.detail: An Amalekite falsely claims to have killed Saul, hoping for a reward, but David has him executed for touching the LORD's anointed, then composes a genuine, grief-stricken lament mourning both Saul and his beloved friend Jonathan.

verses.text: “The beauty of Israel lies slain on your high places! How the mighty have fallen!”

eras.label: Era Two · 2 Samuel 2-3
eras.name: Civil War — Abner's Death
eras.dates: A divided kingdom fights a prolonged civil war between David's supporters and Saul's surviving house, ending with the assassination of Saul's own general

events.title: David Anointed King Over Judah — Civil War Begins
events.detail: David is anointed king over Judah in Hebron while Saul's general Abner installs Ish Bosheth as a rival king over the rest of Israel, and a prolonged war between the two houses begins with a deadly skirmish at the pool of Gibeon.

verses.text: “David was king in Hebron over the people of Judah for seven-and-a-half years.”

events.title: Joab Assassinates Abner
events.detail: As David steadily grows stronger, Abner defects to David's side after a quarrel with Ish Bosheth, but Joab murders him in revenge for his own brother's death, prompting David to publicly mourn Abner and disavow the killing.

verses.text: “Do you not realize that a great leader has fallen this day in Israel?”

eras.label: Era Three · 2 Samuel 4
eras.name: Ish Bosheth Murdered
eras.dates: Saul's remaining rival king is assassinated by his own officers, who expect a reward but receive execution instead

events.title: Ish Bosheth Assassinated — His Killers Executed
events.detail: Two of Ish Bosheth's own officers murder him in his bed hoping for David's favor, but David executes them for killing an innocent man, and gives Ish Bosheth an honorable burial alongside Abner.

verses.text: “When wicked men have killed an innocent man as he slept in his own house, should I not now require his blood from your hands?”

eras.label: Era Four · 2 Samuel 5
eras.name: David King Over All Israel — Jerusalem Captured
eras.dates: With the civil war finally over, all Israel unites behind David, and he captures the previously impregnable stronghold of Jerusalem to make it his capital

events.title: David Captures Jerusalem — the City of David
events.detail: All the tribes of Israel finally unite behind David as king, and he captures the seemingly impregnable Jebusite stronghold of Jerusalem to make it his new capital, defeating the Philistines decisively as his power grows.

verses.text: “David became more and more powerful, for the LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] of Heaven's Armies was with him.”

eras.label: Era Five · 2 Samuel 6
eras.name: The Ark Brought to Jerusalem
eras.dates: A first, deadly attempt to move the ark gives way to a joyful procession into the new capital, marred by Michal's contempt for David's uninhibited worship

events.title: Uzzah Struck Down — David Dances Before the LORD
events.detail: Uzzah is struck dead for touching the ark when the oxen stumble, delaying the ark's move to Jerusalem by three months; when it finally arrives, David dances before it with uninhibited joy, provoking his wife Michal's contempt and a permanent rift between them.

verses.text: “It was before the LORD [Yahweh]! I was celebrating before the LORD [Yahweh], who chose me over your father.”

eras.label: Era Six · 2 Samuel 7
eras.name: The Davidic Covenant
eras.dates: David's wish to build the LORD a permanent temple is redirected into one of the most consequential promises in the Old Testament: an eternal dynasty

events.title: Your House and Your Kingdom Will Stand Before Me Permanently
events.detail: David wants to build a temple, but Nathan relays the LORD's answer: instead of David building God a house, God will build David a dynastic house that will last forever — a covenant promise that becomes the foundation for later Messianic hope.

verses.text: “Your house and your kingdom will stand before me permanently; your throne will be established until perpetuity.”

eras.label: Era Seven · 2 Samuel 8-9
eras.name: David's Victories — Kindness to Mephibosheth
eras.dates: Military conquest on every front is followed by a strikingly personal act of covenant loyalty to Jonathan's crippled son

events.title: David Guaranteed Justice for All His People
events.detail: David subdues the Philistines, Moabites, Arameans, and Edomites in succession, dedicating the plunder to the LORD and establishing a government administration to guarantee justice throughout his growing kingdom.

verses.text: “David reigned over all Israel; he guaranteed justice for all his people.”

events.title: Kindness to Mephibosheth for Jonathan's Sake
events.detail: Remembering his covenant with Jonathan, David seeks out Jonathan's crippled son Mephibosheth and restores his grandfather Saul's land to him, inviting him to eat permanently at the king's own table like one of his sons.

verses.text: “David said to him, ‘Do not be afraid, because I will certainly extend kindness to you for the sake of Jonathan your father.’”

eras.label: Era Eight · 2 Samuel 10
eras.name: War With Ammon and Aram
eras.dates: A diplomatic gesture of sympathy is humiliatingly rejected, escalating into a two-front war that David's army wins decisively

events.title: David's Messengers Humiliated — War With Ammon and Aram
events.detail: The Ammonites humiliate David's sympathy delegation by shaving half their beards and exposing them, triggering a war with hired Aramean mercenaries that Joab and his brother Abishai win decisively on two fronts at once.

verses.text: “Be strong! Let's fight bravely for the sake of our people and the cities of our God! The LORD will do what he decides is best!”

eras.label: Era Nine · 2 Samuel 11
eras.name: Bathsheba and Uriah
eras.dates: The king who refused to harm Saul now arranges the death of one of his own most loyal soldiers to cover up an affair

events.title: David and Bathsheba — Uriah Sent to His Death
events.detail: David sleeps with Bathsheba while her husband Uriah is at war, and when a cover-up scheme fails because Uriah's loyalty won't let him enjoy home comforts while his fellow soldiers camp in the field, David arranges to have him killed in battle.

verses.text: “She became his wife and she bore him a son. But what David had done upset the LORD [Yahweh].”

eras.label: Era Ten · 2 Samuel 12
eras.name: You Are That Man — Nathan's Rebuke
eras.dates: A parable about a stolen lamb exposes the king's own crime to his face, triggering genuine repentance but not escaping real consequences

events.title: You Are That Man! — I Have Sinned Against the LORD
events.detail: Nathan's parable about a rich man stealing a poor man's only lamb tricks David into condemning himself before revealing 'you are that man'; David confesses immediately and is forgiven, but the child born from the affair dies, and Bathsheba later gives birth to Solomon.

verses.text: “David exclaimed to Nathan, ‘I have sinned against the LORD [Yahweh]!’ Nathan replied, ‘The LORD [Yahweh] has forgiven your sin. You are not going to die.’”

eras.label: Era Eleven · 2 Samuel 13
eras.name: Amnon and Tamar
eras.dates: A crime within David's own household goes unpunished, planting the seed of a devastating fratricide two years later

events.title: Amnon Rapes Tamar — Absalom's Revenge
events.detail: David's son Amnon rapes his half-sister Tamar and then discards her; David is furious but takes no action, so two years later Tamar's full brother Absalom has Amnon murdered at a feast and flees into exile.

verses.text: “Absalom said nothing to Amnon, either bad or good, yet Absalom hated Amnon because he had humiliated his sister Tamar.”

eras.label: Era Twelve · 2 Samuel 14
eras.name: Absalom's Return Engineered
eras.dates: Joab stages an elaborate parable to maneuver David into recalling his exiled son, though reconciliation remains incomplete

events.title: The Wise Woman of Tekoa — Absalom Recalled but Kept at a Distance
events.detail: Joab arranges for a wise woman to tell David a fictional parable that maneuvers him into recalling Absalom from exile, but David refuses to see his son face to face for two more years, leaving the reconciliation dangerously incomplete.

verses.text: “We must die, and are like water spilled on the ground that cannot be gathered up again. But God does not take away life; instead he devises ways for the banished to be restored.”

eras.label: Era Thirteen · 2 Samuel 15
eras.name: Absalom's Rebellion Begins
eras.dates: Years of quietly winning public favor at the city gate erupt into open rebellion, forcing David to flee his own capital

events.title: Absalom Steals the Hearts of Israel — David Flees Jerusalem
events.detail: After years of positioning himself as a more accessible judge than his father, Absalom launches open rebellion from Hebron; David flees Jerusalem in grief, sending the ark back to the city and planting Hushai as a secret counter-agent in Absalom's court.

verses.text: “Take the ark of God back to the city. If I find favor in the LORD's [Yahweh's] sight he will bring me back.”

eras.label: Era Fourteen · 2 Samuel 16-17
eras.name: Shimei's Curse — Ahithophel Versus Hushai
eras.dates: A cursing relative of Saul is left alone by David's own choice, while a battle of competing advice determines the rebellion's entire trajectory

events.title: Shimei Curses David — Absalom Takes Ahithophel's Advice
events.detail: A relative of Saul named Shimei curses and throws stones at the fleeing David, who refuses to let his men kill him, accepting it as possibly from the LORD; meanwhile Absalom publicly claims his father's concubines on the advice of Ahithophel.

verses.text: “What do we have in common, you sons of Zeruiah? If he curses because the LORD has said to him, ‘Curse David!,’ who can say to him, ‘Why have you done this?’”

events.title: Hushai's Advice Chosen — the LORD Frustrates Ahithophel
events.detail: Absalom rejects Ahithophel's sound military advice in favor of Hushai's delaying counsel, a decision the narrator explicitly attributes to the LORD's own intervention to bring disaster on Absalom; the humiliated Ahithophel goes home and hangs himself.

verses.text: “The LORD had decided to frustrate the sound advice of Ahithophel, so that the LORD could bring disaster on Absalom.”

eras.label: Era Fifteen · 2 Samuel 18-19
eras.name: Absalom's Death — My Son, My Son, Absalom
eras.dates: The rebellion's decisive battle ends with the prince caught by his own hair in an oak tree, and a father's grief that overshadows his own victory

events.title: Absalom Caught in an Oak Tree — Joab Kills Him Against David's Order
events.detail: Despite David's explicit order to deal gently with Absalom, Joab kills him when he's found helplessly caught by his hair in an oak tree; the news reaches David not as victory but as devastating personal loss.

verses.text: “The king became very upset… as he went he said, ‘My son, Absalom! My son, my son, Absalom! If only I could have died in your place!’” (Numbered 18:33 in most English translations.)

events.title: David Returns to Jerusalem
events.detail: Joab rebukes David for grieving over an enemy while ignoring the men who saved his life, and David returns to Jerusalem, navigating reconciliation with Shimei, Mephibosheth, and the aging Barzillai, while tension simmers between Judah and the rest of Israel over who gets credit for restoring him.

verses.text: “You seem to love your enemies and hate your friends!”

eras.label: Era Sixteen · 2 Samuel 20
eras.name: Sheba's Revolt
eras.dates: The tension between Israel and Judah erupts into a second, smaller rebellion, ended by a wise woman's negotiated surrender of a single head

events.title: Sheba's Revolt — a Wise Woman Ends the Siege
events.detail: A Benjaminite named Sheba leads Israel away from David in a second rebellion; Joab murders his rival Amasa along the way, and the revolt ends when a wise woman in besieged Abel negotiates the surrender of Sheba's head alone.

verses.text: “The woman went to all the people with her wise advice and they cut off Sheba's head and threw it out to Joab.”

eras.label: Era Seventeen · 2 Samuel 21
eras.name: The Gibeonites Avenged — Philistine Giants Fall
eras.dates: An old, unresolved national guilt over Saul's broken treaty must be settled before a famine lifts, followed by a series of battles against Goliath's own kin

events.title: A Famine Ends After the Gibeonites Are Avenged
events.detail: A three-year famine is traced back to Saul's broken treaty with the Gibeonites; seven of Saul's descendants are executed to make amends, and Rizpah's faithful vigil over their bodies moves David to finally give Saul and Jonathan a proper burial.

verses.text: “After they had done everything that the king had commanded, God responded to their prayers for the land.”

events.title: Goliath's Kin Fall to David's Men
events.detail: In a series of battles against Philistine giants descended from Rapha, David's exhausted men finally insist he stop personally fighting, and his soldiers kill four giants including the brother of Goliath himself.

verses.text: “You will not go out to battle with us again! You must not extinguish the lamp of Israel!”

eras.label: Era Eighteen · 2 Samuel 22
eras.name: David's Song of Deliverance
eras.dates: A lifetime of rescue from enemies, including Saul himself, is celebrated in an extended song of praise, nearly identical to Psalm 18

events.title: The LORD Is My Rock, My Fortress, My Deliverer
events.detail: In a sweeping victory song (preserved nearly identically as Psalm 18), David celebrates the LORD as rock, fortress, and deliverer, recounting rescue from death itself and closing with a promise of faithfulness to David's line forever.

verses.text: “He said: ‘The LORD [Yahweh] is my high ridge, my stronghold, my deliverer.’”

eras.label: Era Nineteen · 2 Samuel 23
eras.name: David's Last Words — the Mighty Men
eras.dates: A final poetic oracle gives way to a roster honoring the elite warriors whose exploits defined David's reign

events.title: David's Final Words — the Roster of Mighty Men
events.detail: David's last recorded oracle reflects on just rule under the fear of God, followed by a detailed honor roll of his elite warriors and their individual feats of courage, including three who risked their lives just to bring him a drink of water.

verses.text: “These are the final words of David: ‘The oracle of David son of Jesse… Israel's beloved singer of songs.’”

eras.label: Era Twenty · 2 Samuel 24
eras.name: The Census and the Plague
eras.dates: The book closes with a national census that provokes divine judgment, resolved at the very threshing floor that would become the future temple site

events.title: David's Census — the Threshing Floor of Araunah
events.detail: David orders a census that provokes divine judgment through plague; when the destroying angel reaches Jerusalem, David buys Araunah's threshing floor to build an altar there and stop the plague — the very site that would later become the temple.

verses.text: “David said to Gad, ‘I am very upset! I prefer that we be attacked by the LORD [Yahweh], for his mercy is great.’”
